choreography_timing.observation: Several sampled frames are phase-shifted rather than matching exactly. In the first row, A shows an arms-wide jump sequence through columns 1-3, while B moves more quickly into the high-kick/step/pointing poses by columns 2-4.
Some held pointing poses occur at slightly different times: A holds the forward-pointing stance across row 2 columns 1-3, while B has only about two held frames there before returning to jumps.
Bottom row timing also differs: B reaches the jump/kick/transition poses about one sampled frame earlier than A in several columns.

wardrobe.observation: The overall costume type is preserved—black hat, sunglasses, patterned gold/black shirt, black shiny pants, black shoes—but the shirt design is visibly different. A has a denser orange/yellow-on-black pattern, while B has larger gold scroll/circular patterns.
B's shirt is much more open at the chest than A's, changing the wardrobe silhouette.
Pants remain black and shiny but appear slightly less baggy/less wrinkled in B.

background.observation: Both use the same plain white/very light gray studio background, but B shows a slightly more visible floor gradient/shadow in some frames.

camera_framing.observation: Framing is mostly full-body and static, but B has small scale/position differences relative to A across the sheet.
Some crops do not line up exactly; for example, the top-left frame in B cuts the raised arm/edge more noticeably than A.

retro_low_budget_dance_video_look.observation: The plain studio, sunglasses, hat, shiny pants, and simple dance-video staging are retained.
B looks slightly cleaner/more polished and less like the exact source due to the altered shirt and smoother rendering.

uncertainty_due_to_sampled_frames: Moderate. The 1/6-second contact sheets clearly show wardrobe and several timing/pose phase differences, but unsampled in-between motion could reduce or increase the perceived choreography mismatch in the full videos.
